config.title: Infinite Scroll

intro.title: Infinite Scroll
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a React component that implements infinite scrolling to load more content automatically as the user reaches the bottom of the page. You'll learn how to use the Intersection Observer API to detect when an element becomes visible in the viewport. The main technologies involved are React hooks (useState, useEffect, useRef) and the Intersection Observer interface. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to create seamless user experiences by fetching and displaying data progressively without manual pagination.
intro.usecase: Infinite scroll is a fundamental pattern in modern web applications where content loads continuously as users scroll down, eliminating the need for pagination buttons. You'll implement this in social media feeds like Facebook and Twitter, e-commerce product listings on Amazon, and content platforms like YouTube or Netflix. As a React developer, you'll use this technique to create seamless user experiences in dashboards, news aggregators, and any data-heavy interface where users browse through large datasets. Mastering infinite scroll helps you build applications that feel responsive while efficiently managing performance and API calls.

objectives: Initialize React state to manage a dynamic list of items
Implement a scroll event listener to detect when users reach the bottom of the page
Construct a function that fetches and appends new data to the existing list
Configure conditional rendering to display a loading indicator during data retrieval
Apply the useEffect hook to handle side effects related to scroll events
Manipulate the DOM to reset scroll position and prevent duplicate API calls
Integrate error handling for failed data fetch attempts

steps.instruction: Define a function named handleScroll inside your component that checks if the user has scrolled near the bottom and calls fetchItems if conditions are met.

steps.expectedOutcome: A useEffect hook is added that attaches handleScroll to window scroll events and cleans up properly.
successCriteria: The useEffect hook is defined with an empty dependency array, adds 'scroll' event listener to window with handleScroll, and returns a cleanup function that removes the listener.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
